problem:
A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration $a(t)=2\operatorname{sin}⁡t,$ where $a(t)$ is measured in ${\text{m/s}}^{2}$ and $t$ is measured in seconds. Find the speed of the particle at the moment $t=\frac{\pi }{3}\,\text{s}$ given that the particle has velocity $v=\frac{1}{2}\,\text{m/s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}.$

The speed at the moment $t=\frac{\pi }{3}\,\text{s}$ is
{{field-1}} $\,\text{m/s}.$
worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int 2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & =-2\operatorname{cos}⁡t+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(0)=\frac{1}{2}.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} & =-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)+C \\ \frac{1}{2} & =-2+C \\ C & =\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=\frac{5}{2}-2\operatorname{cos}⁡t.$

We evaluate the velocity at time $t=\frac{\pi }{3}\,\text{s}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(\frac{\pi }{3}) & =\frac{5}{2}-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}) \\  & =\frac{5}{2}-2(\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\,\text{m/s}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the speed is equal to $|v(t)|,$ we conclude that the speed of the particle is $\frac{3}{2}\,\text{m/s}.$
